svg.aria-label: How to write ಝ: 5 strokes · 4 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing ಝ
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ಝ (kannada), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansKannada-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-jha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಝ, 53 frames, 5.3 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kannada-alphabet-jha.gif>. Source note on variation: The CC BY-SA 4.0 animation writes ಝ in five pen-down runs: the round bowl, counterclockwise from its upper left (frames 0–10); after a lift, the top bar from left to right curling up into the hook (frames 13–21); after a second lift, the middle arm from its foot, round its base and up its right side, curling in at the top (frames 24–29); after a third lift, the right arm drawn the same way (frames 33–38); after a fourth lift, the tail below, drawn downward (frames 42–43). The frames were read from a mirror copy (225×196, 53 frames); no listed size for the Commons file was available to compare it with, so only the slug and the frames were checked. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Kannada outline rather than copying the animation's handwritten proportions; in that outline the bowl's top is fused into the bar, as in ರ, so the closing movement runs along the lower part of the bar's ink and the bar retraces it, and the tail is a straight tapered bar, but the four-lift order remains the same.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 strokes · 4 pen lifts · 9 movements

text.tspan: and curl in at the top
